chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from al-Nadr ibn Suwayd and Safwan from Ibn Sinan and Hammad from Ibn al-Mughira from Ibn Sinan from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who performed Tamattu' but could not find a sacrificial animal. He said: 'Let him fast three days, which are not the days of Tashriq, but he must remain in Mecca until he fasts them, and seven days when he returns to his family.' And he mentioned the hadith of Budayl ibn Warqa'.

key_terms.اَلتَّشْرِيقِ: Days of Tashriq (11th, 12th, 13th of Dhu al-Hijjah)
key_terms.بُدَيْلِ بْنِ وَرْقَاءَ: Budayl ibn Warqa' (a companion of the Imams)
key_terms.تَمَتَّعَ: Performed Tamattu' (a type of Hajj combining Umrah and Hajj)

ai.seo_question: What is the expiation for a pilgrim who cannot afford a sacrificial animal during Tamattu'?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific fidya for a Mutamatti' pilgrim lacking a sacrificial animal, emphasizing the distinct location of the first three fasting days within Mecca to avoid the days of Tashriq. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise ritual timing and the practical application of Quranic verses, linking the expiation to the broader legal framework of Hajj obligations.
